source_text: Quot igitur patrocinia naturae, quot privilegia gratiae, quot solemnia disciplinae, figurae, praestructiones, precationes religionem aquae ordinaverunt? Primo quidem, cum populus de Aegypto libere expeditus, vim regis Aegypti, per aquam transgressus, evadit, ipsum regem cum totis copiis aqua exstinxit. Quae figura manifestior in Baptimi sacramento? Liberantur de saeculo nationes per aquam scilicet, et diabolum, dominatorem pristinum, in aqua oppressum derelinquunt. Item aqua de amaritudinis vitio in suum commodum suavitatis Mosei ligno remediatur. Lignum illud erat Christus, venenatae et amarae retro naturae venas insaluberrimas, aquas Baptismi, scilicet, ex sese remedians. Haec est aqua, quae de comite petra populo defluebat. Si enim petra Christus, sine dubio aqua in Christo Baptismum videmus benedici. Quanta aquae gratia penes Deum et Christum ejus est ad Baptismi confirmationem. Nunquam sine aqua Christus, siquidem et ipse aqua tinguitur. Prima rudimenta potestatis suae, vocatus ad nuptias, aqua auspicatur. Cum sermonem facit, sitientes ad aquam suam invitat sempiternam. Cum de agape docet, aquae calicem, fratri oblatum, inter opera dilectionis probat. Apud puteum vires resumit; super aquam incedit libenter, transfretat; aquam discentibus ministrat; perseverat testimonium Baptismi usque ad passionem; cum deditur in crucem, aqua intervenit, sciunt Pilati manus; cum vulneratur, aqua de latere prorumpit, scit lancea militis.
pass_a_gloss: How many defenses of nature, how many privileges of grace, how many solemnities of discipline, figures, prefigurings, prayers have ordained the religion of water? First, indeed, when the people, having been freely led out of Egypt, having crossed through the water, escaped the force of the king of Egypt, the water destroyed the king himself with all his forces. What figure is more manifest in the sacrament of Baptism? Nations are freed from the world through water, and they leave behind the devil, their former ruler, oppressed in the water. Also, the water is remedied from the fault of bitterness by the wood of Moses for its own benefit of sweetness. That wood was Christ, remedying the most unhealthy veins of a poisonous and bitter nature, namely the waters of Baptism, from himself. This is the water which flowed from the rock, the companion of the people. For if the rock is Christ, without a doubt we see Baptism blessed in Christ. How great is the grace of water with God and His Christ for the confirmation of Baptism. Christ is never without water, since He Himself is also baptized with water. The first beginnings of His power are inaugurated with water, when He is invited to a wedding. When He preaches, He invites the thirsty to His eternal water. When He teaches about love, He approves the cup of water, offered to His brother, among the works of love. At the well He resumes His strength; He walks freely upon the water, crosses over; He serves water to His disciples; He persists in the testimony of Baptism up to His passion; when He is handed over to the cross, water intervenes, as Pilate's hands know; when He is wounded, water bursts forth from His side, as the soldier's lance knows.
pass_b_english: How many defenses of nature, how many privileges of grace, how many solemnities of discipline, figures, prefigurings, and prayers have established the religion of water? First, when the people were freely led out of Egypt and crossed through the water, they escaped the force of the king of Egypt, and the water destroyed the king himself with all his forces (Exodus 14:28). What figure could be more manifest in the sacrament of Baptism? Nations are freed from the world through water, and they leave behind the devil, their former ruler, crushed in the water. Also, the water was remedied from the fault of bitterness by the wood of Moses for its own benefit of sweetness (Exodus 15:25). That wood was Christ, healing the most unhealthy veins of a poisonous and bitter nature — namely, the waters of Baptism — from himself. This is the water that flowed from the companion rock for the people (Exodus 17:6). For if the rock is Christ, without a doubt we see Baptism blessed in Christ. How great is the grace of water with God and his Christ for the confirmation of Baptism! Christ is never without water, since he himself was baptized with water. The first beginnings of his power were inaugurated with water when he was invited to a wedding (John 2:1-11). When he preaches, he invites the thirsty to his eternal water (John 4:14). When he teaches about love, he approves the cup of water, offered to his brother, among the works of love. At the well he resumes his strength; he walks freely upon the water and crosses over; he serves water to his disciples; he persists in the testimony of Baptism up to his passion. When he is handed over to the cross, water intervenes — Pilate's hands know this. When he is wounded, water bursts forth from his side — the soldier's lance knows this (John 19:34).
